results.name: Nscale Acquires Anyscale in $1.65 Billion Deal to Build Full-Stack AI Hyperscaler
results.content:
London-based AI cloud platform Nscale announced a definitive agreement on July 30, 2026, to acquire Anyscale, the software company created by the developers of the open-source Ray framework.
Nscale stated it will join the PyTorch Foundation as part of the acquisition agreement. The transaction follows several capital commitments by Nscale during 2026. Nscale entered into a letter of intent with Microsoft in March 2026 covering over 1 gigawatt of power capacity. Nscale committed $2.5 billion to UK data center investments and secured a $900 million revolving credit facility in July 2026, syndicated through banks including J.P. Morgan, Goldman Sachs, and Morgan Stanley. Anyscale previously secured $100 million in funding at a $1 billion valuation during its Series C round in 2021.
Anyscale will retain its independent brand, and its 200-person workforce will join London-based Nscale. London-based AI cloud platform Nscale announced a definitive agreement on July 30, 2026, to acquire Anyscale, the software company created by the developers of the open-source Ray framework.
The transaction combines Nscale’s infrastructure assets (including power generation, data center real estate, and GPU compute clusters) with Anyscale’s workload orchestration software. Official corporate announcements from both entities did not reveal the financial purchase price. Bloomberg reported the deal valuation at approximately $1.65 billion, citing a source familiar with the matter. The transaction is scheduled to close in the second half of 2026, pending regulatory approvals and standard closing conditions.
Anyscale founders created Ray, a widely adopted open-source framework used to scale Python and AI workloads. Governance of the Ray project transferred to the PyTorch Foundation under the Linux Foundation in October 2025. The open-source Ray framework remains community-governed and separate from Nscale's commercial acquisition.

By bundling GPU‑heavy compute with a cloud‑neutral orchestration layer, Nscale can differentiate on performance while still courting multi‑cloud customers, a balance that could set a new standard for AI‑centric SaaS offerings. For operators, the acquisition signals that vertical integration—combining hardware, power, and software—may become a competitive necessity to win enterprise AI contracts that demand both scalability and cost predictability.
This vertical integration mirrors moves in other cloud‑adjacent markets, such as Snowflake’s acquisition of Streamlit to embed data‑app development directly into its warehouse. The real test will be whether Nscale can maintain the promised platform neutrality. If customers perceive a performance bias toward Nscale’s own hardware, the value proposition could shift from “neutral SaaS” to a de‑facto lock‑in, echoing early criticisms of proprietary cloud services. However, the company’s commitment to keep Anyscale’s brand and support for AWS, GCP, and Azure may mitigate that risk, especially for enterprises that have already spread workloads across multiple clouds for resilience and cost arbitrage.
Smaller orchestration startups may become acquisition targets for larger neoclouds seeking to differentiate on performance. Meanwhile, hyperscalers will likely double‑down on their own AI‑native services, forcing them to compete on more than just raw compute pricing. For SaaS operators, the Nscale‑Anyscale model offers a template: combine deep hardware expertise with a flexible, developer‑centric software layer to create a defensible moat that is hard to replicate without comparable capital investment.

Nscale, a full-stack AI cloud platform, today announced it has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Anyscale, the platform for scaling any AI workload - data processing, training, inference and reinforcement learning - across thousands of GPUs.  
The acquisition brings together two highly complementary companies. Nscale supplies the infrastructure – GPUs, data centers, power – and the software that AI runs on. Anyscale brings the software layer that machine learning engineers and AI platform teams use to run their workloads. Anyscale's software layer will expand Nscale's existing software capabilities to further extend Nscale's full stack AI cloud offering, from power to production AI.

From healthcare to e-commerce to robotics, this full stack offering will help companies speed up image and document processing, fine-tune LLMs on their proprietary data, and deploy AI agents in-house using open-source models.
Anyscale will continue to operate under its brand and serve its existing customers as it does today. Customers will remain free to choose the infrastructure on which they run their AI workloads, and over time will gain the additional option of running the Anyscale software layer on Nscale's full stack AI platform. Anyscale's entire team — approximately 200 people across the United States, Europe and India — will join Nscale as part of the acquisition.  
Anyscale was founded by the creators of Ray, the open-source standard for building and scaling distributed AI applications. In 2025, Ray was donated to the PyTorch Foundation and remains open source and community governed. Nscale will join the PyTorch Foundation, reinforcing its commitment to Ray's long-term success alongside the tens of thousands of developers in the broader open-source community.  
Read the full press release [here](https://www.nscale.com/press-releases/nscale-acquires-anyscale).

# Anyscale platform release notes - May 2026  
# Anyscale platform release notes - May 2026  
Use this page to learn about new features and improvements to the Anyscale platform released in May 2026, including the Anyscale console, CLI, and SDK.  
To learn about new features added as part of Ray releases, see [Ray release highlights](https://github.com/ray-project/ray/releases).
## Task and actor dashboards are now generally available on AKS, EKS, and GKE[](#task-dash-ga)  
**May 4, 2026**  
The Anyscale task and actor dashboards are now generally available on Anyscale clouds backed by AKS, EKS, and GKE. Anyscale also extended the supporting [system cluster](https://docs.anyscale.com/clouds/system-cluster) to other Kubernetes providers in beta release. See [Anyscale task dashboard](https://docs.anyscale.com/monitoring/task-dashboard) and [Anyscale actor dashboard](https://docs.anyscale.com/monitoring/actor-dashboard).
## Multi-version services move to private beta[](#multi-version-private-beta)  
**May 4, 2026**  
`anyscale service deploy --versions` now requires Anyscale to enable the `enable-multi-version-services` feature flag for your organization. The feature is supported only on Anyscale clouds backed by virtual machines (VMs) on AWS. To request access, contact [Anyscale support](https://docs.anyscale.com/release-notes/platform/2026/may/mailto:support@anyscale.com).  
Anyscale enforces this flag server-side, so the requirement applies to all CLI and SDK versions. Operations on existing multi-version services, including traffic weight updates, restarts, in-place upgrades, and rollbacks, continue to work without the feature flag. Anyscale CLI/SDK 0.26.100 adds a translated error message for organizations without the flag enabled. See [Version 0.26.100 release notes](https://docs.anyscale.com/release-notes/cli-sdk#0-26-100).
